source.title: Matching Ranks Over Probability Yields Truly Deep Safety Alignment

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present; the text is coherent.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a different attack, Rank-Assisted Prefilling, can recover harmful content from models trained for deep safety alignment, and whether a new training method reduces that vulnerability.
record.gate_note: The study tests RAP, ordinary prefilling, GCG suffix attacks, and PRESTO's effect on those attacks. It also reports entropy plots relevant to its explanation of the data-augmentation objective. It does not test harmful-example fine-tuning alone, benign fine-tuning, per-token KL concentration, or safety localization in a small set of weights. Attention-pattern plots and the attention-suppression/PFA-loss plot are mechanistic or proxy analyses, not direct behavioral outcomes; they are not recorded as behavioral rows. Cited results from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: Its own results show that the data-augmentation deepening fix (V7) blocks ordinary prefilling but fails against rank-assisted prefilling (RAP). RAP recovers most of the original model's harmfulness, which is a direct argument that the deepening fix is partial. It also re-measures ordinary prefilling on Llama 2 7B Chat (V4) and tests PRESTO, a new deepening method, against RAP and GCG.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that data-augmentation deep alignment is superficial: RAP easily recovers substantial harmful content. PRESTO, an attention regularizer derived from push-forward alignment, makes RAP much harder (up to 4.7x safety improvement) with utility within about 1%. Against GCG, PRESTO further halves the score relative to data augmentation alone.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the data-augmentation deep-safety-alignment approach as a baseline and adds PRESTO attention regularization; applies the baseline to newer models as well as evaluating the Llama 2 checkpoint.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack method (ordinary prefilling, RAP, GCG), RAP top-k value, tested model, human attacker category versus AutoRAP, and whether PRESTO is used.

fits_no_version.finding: After data augmentation, next-token entropy after a harmful prefill is sharpened toward the original model's prompt-only distribution. Low-probability harmful tokens are left highly ranked, which the authors call 'gaming' the KL objective.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Probability-matching deepening objectives leave harmful tokens high in rank, so deep alignment can stay rank-shallow.

fits_no_version.finding: In the data-augmented model, attention to harmful prefill tokens persists. PRESTO suppresses it in later layers (Figures 11–12).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Robust deepening requires that later-layer attention ignore the harmful prefill.

record.peer_reviewed: Trustworthy AI for Good (AI4GOOD) Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning; PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: Human RAP evaluation uses three attacker categories and a limited prompt sample; AutoRAP depends on a separately trained refusal-token classifier. Several cross-model RAP outcomes are presented only in figures. The entropy evidence is plotted without numerical values and does not isolate the proposed objective mechanism causally. GCG is evaluated only on Llama 2.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning is used only as a tool, to produce jailbroken models that generate the training data. Its effect is not measured as a result.
All of V2: benign fine-tuning is not tested.
All of V3: per-token KL divergence across response positions is not measured.
The decoding-parameter exploit is only cited, not run. Ordinary prefilling of an undeepened model is tested only on Llama 2.
All of V5: localization of safety in parameters is not tested.
Why the original alignment is shallow is not tested. The entropy analysis concerns the deepening objective instead.

missing.what: Utility cost of deepening (MT-Bench and GSM-8K) for the original, data-augmented and data-augmented+PRESTO versions of three models. Data augmentation lowers Gemma's GSM-8K from 90.22% to 86.35%; PRESTO stays within about 1%.
Human RAP time per selected token rises under PRESTO across models.
About 97% of probability mass sits on the refusal token 'I' after a prefill in the data-augmented model, while harmful tokens remain in the top 10.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 'challenges' label is removed. Ordinary prefilling failing on the deepened model is V7 evidence, not V4 evidence. The V6 label is dropped because the entropy rows are proxy measures about the deepening objective, not about why the original alignment is shallow. The human RAP results use one participant per category, with novices differing by model and the expert being an author. Table 1 human RAP covers 52 prompts, while the prefilling comparison uses all 313.

versions.untested_parts: Whether fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples alone removes refusal.
Whether benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Decoding changes are not evaluated. The attack results concern ordinary prefilling, RAP token selection, and GCG; they do not test every type of compliant opening or suffix.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The proposed explanation is not isolated through a causal comparison of alternative data-augmentation objectives; the entropy evidence is reported for Llama 2 7B Chat.
The study does not directly measure safety behavior distributed across response positions. It evaluates robustness to RAP and GCG, on the reported models and settings.
